criteria.check: Checked R50 across src/cma/report.py:1-132, src/cma/cli.py:936-973, src/cma/review/summary.py:92-350, src/cma/metrics.py:758-975, src/cma/overrides.py:372-552, src/cma/store.py:260-280, tests/test_report.py:1-174, and runner logs (contracts-4.log:716-721). Found three major defects in traced detection (false-positive exit 1 on valid missed-VAT M13; false-negative exit 0 on zero-valued derived figures/cells and reasonless n/a monthly cells) and error/read-only handling (unhandled CaseStoreError/CaseRootInGit/OSError crashing cma report and hiding other cases, plus ensure_root chmod side effect), plus two minor findings (unproven read-only claim in claim.json and coupled _overrides/entries error handling losing signed_off).

findings.claim: False-positive untraced flag and exit 1 on valid cases with vat_stagger set and missed VAT payments: _untraced flags any figure with value != 0 and lines == 0, but metrics.compute produces M13 (Late or missed VAT payments) with value >= 1 and evidence == [] when no HMRC VAT payment lines exist in the statement (src/cma/metrics.py:758-770, 861-862).
findings.repro: Create a case with vat_stagger: 1 in case.yaml, import a valid statement covering 2026-01-01 to 2026-06-30 with no HMRC VAT payment lines (e.g. two STRIPE credits on 2026-01-05 and 2026-06-15), and run `cma report`. M13 has value=1 and evidence=[], so report.report()[0] returns traced=False, untraced=['main:M13'] and `cma report` exits with code 1 on a valid, fully traced case.

findings.claim: False-negative traced=True and exit 0 for zero-valued figures/cells that must cite lines and for n/a monthly cells without a reason: _nothing_to_cite treats value == 0 as needing no lines for every figure and monthly cell, missing untraced derived figures/cells that must always cite lines at zero (M5, M27, M16, M26, M9, M10, M28, M4, M1, and monthly average_balance, lowest_balance, days_overdrawn per R11/R12/P2); additionally line 47 never checks `cell['value'] is None and not cell.get('note')` for n/a monthly cells.
findings.repro: 1) On a case using BODY from tests/test_report.py (where monthly days_overdrawn is 0) or a case with 0% unexplained share (M26=0.0), monkeypatch metrics.monthly_summary to set row.days_overdrawn.evidence = [] (or metrics.compute to set M26.evidence = []). `cma report` returns traced=True, untraced=[] and exits 0. 2) Monkeypatch metrics.monthly_summary to set a monthly cell's value=None, note=None, evidence=[]. `cma report` returns traced=True, untraced=[] and exits 0.

findings.claim: Unhandled crashes on partial failure or refused case roots, and filesystem mutation on read: report.report() calls store.case_folder(case_id, root) outside case_report's exception handler, and cli.py:951 omits `with _case_errors():`. A case purged or losing case.yaml between case_ids() and store.case_folder() aborts the report with CaseStoreError and hides all remaining cases; an unignored git case root or unreadable root dumps an unhandled traceback; and store.case_folder() calls store.ensure_root() on every case, running os.chmod(0o700) on root and root/cases (violating the read-only claim and failing on read-only mounts).
findings.repro: 1) Create two cases A and B; delete A/case.yaml (or purge A) after case_ids() returns [A, B] and before store.case_folder(A) runs. report.report() raises CaseStoreError and never reports B. 2) Point CMA_HOME inside a git repo that does not ignore it, place a case folder under cases/<hex16>/case.yaml, and run `cma report`: it crashes with an unhandled CaseRootInGit traceback instead of a clean refusal. 3) `chmod 0o755` on CMA_HOME containing a case and run `cma report`: directory permissions are mutated back to 0o700.

findings.claim: Unproven claim in claim.json: claim #2 ('cma report writes nothing. Two runs leave every file under the case root byte for byte unchanged') cites `PYTHONPATH=src python <scratchpad>/ro.py`, which is not in the repository and was not executed by any configured runner tier. No test in tests/test_report.py verifies that `cma report` leaves files and permissions under CMA_HOME unchanged.
findings.repro: Inspect claim.json claim #2 and tests/test_report.py:1-174; neither specified-3.log nor contracts-4.log contains a read-only/idempotency test for `cma report`. Prove by adding a `@pytest.mark.contracts` test in tests/test_report.py that hashes all files and records directory modes under CMA_HOME before and after two `cma report` invocations, and running `python -m pytest -v -rs --tier-results` and `python tools/tier_check.py contracts`.

findings.claim: Coupled post-summary error handling and multi-read race in case_report: _overrides(folder) and caselog.for_case(folder).entries() share one try block (lines 102-109), so a corrupt statement CSV causes overrides.listing(folder) to raise StatementError on line 103 before line 104 reads the intact case log, reporting signed_off=None instead of True. Conversely, if lines 103-104 fail after case_summary succeeded, state/traced/reconciled/signed_off are reset to refused/None while accounts, queue_lines, indicator_lines, and unexplained_share remain populated; separate entries() reads across case_summary, _overrides, and line 104 also allow concurrent writes to yield a mixed row.
findings.repro: Create and sign off a case as in tests/test_report.py:_signed_case, then overwrite folder/'statements'/'main.csv' with invalid CSV bytes ('bad'). Call report.case_report(folder, case_id): log.jsonl is intact with event 'signed_off', yet out['signed_off'] is None instead of True because _overrides(folder) raised StatementError at report.py:103.
